s: Which one of the following statements is incorrect with reference to megalithic burials in Andhra?
o: Tirupati has the largest anthropomorphic burial site collection.
Many numbers of cist burials were found in Visakhapatnam District.
Sarcophagus burials are more in number in Chittoor and Anantapuram districts.
Krishna and Chittoor districts contained many numbers of dolmen burials.
x:
The Megalithic Culture (Iron Age) of Andhra Pradesh is represented by various burial types such as cists, dolmens, sarcophagi, cairn circles and anthropomorphic burials. Their distribution varies from district to district, and questions on these burial types are frequently asked in APPSC examinations.
Option (1): Tirupati has the largest anthropomorphic burial site collection. This statement is correct. The Tirupati region, particularly around Chandragiri and nearby localities, contains one of the largest collections of anthropomorphic megaliths (human-shaped stone memorials) in India. These are unique memorial stones erected during the Megalithic period and represent an important archaeological feature of southern Andhra Pradesh.
Option (2): Many numbers of cist burials were found in Visakhapatnam District. This statement is correct. Cist burials are stone-lined rectangular burial chambers constructed using large stone slabs. They are widely distributed in Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts, making the statement factually correct.
Option (3): Sarcophagus burials are more in number in Chittoor and Anantapuram districts. This statement is correct. Sarcophagus burials consist of terracotta coffins, often supported by legs. These burials are predominantly found in Chittoor and Anantapuram districts and represent a distinctive feature of the Megalithic culture in southern Andhra Pradesh.
Option (4): Krishna and Chittoor districts contained many numbers of dolmen burials. This statement is incorrect. Dolmens are table-like stone structures made of upright stone slabs covered by a capstone. In Andhra Pradesh, dolmens are mainly concentrated in Kurnool, Kadapa and Anantapuram districts, not in Krishna district. Therefore, mentioning Krishna district makes the statement incorrect.
Exam Note:
• Anthropomorphic Burials – Tirupati region
• Cist Burials – Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam
• Dolmens – Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapuram
• Sarcophagus Burials – Chittoor, Anantapuram

This question tests knowledge of Satavahana literature.
Statement (A): This statement is correct. Gatha Saptasathi (Gaha Sattasai) was compiled by King Hala, a Satavahana ruler. It consists of nearly 700 Prakrit verses dealing mainly with love, romance, rural life, women's emotions and nature. It is regarded as one of the finest literary works of ancient India written in Maharashtri Prakrit.
Statement (B): This statement is incorrect. Gunadya wrote the famous Brihatkatha in Paisachi language, not in Sanskrit. The original work has been lost, but later Sanskrit adaptations such as Kathasaritsagara (Somadeva) and Brihatkatha Manjari (Kshemendra) were based on it. Since Statement (A) is true and Statement (B) is false, the correct answer is Option (3).

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect with reference to the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri?
o: In their inscriptions, Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri had described themselves as the descendants of Ikshvakus of Ayodhya.
Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri had matrimonial ties with Sakas/Western Satraps of Ujjain.
Veerapurushadatta's reign is considered as the golden age of Buddhism in Andhra.
x:
The Ikshvakus ruled from Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda) after the decline of the Satavahanas and played a major role in promoting Buddhism in Andhra Pradesh.
Option (1): This statement is correct. The Puranas refer to the Ikshvakus as Sri Parvathiyas, as they ruled the region around Sri Parvata (Nagarjunakonda).
Option (2): This statement is incorrect. Although the dynasty adopted the prestigious name Ikshvaku, their inscriptions do not explicitly claim descent from the Ikshvakus of Ayodhya. Historians generally consider the name to have been adopted for political prestige rather than as a proven genealogical claim.
Option (3): This statement is correct. The Ikshvaku rulers established matrimonial alliances with the Sakas (Western Kshatrapas) of Ujjain, strengthening their political influence.
Option (4): This statement is correct. The reign of Veerapurushadatta witnessed extensive patronage of Buddhism. Numerous monasteries, stupas and Buddhist establishments were constructed at Nagarjunakonda through donations made by the royal family, especially queens and royal women. Therefore, his reign is regarded as the golden age of Buddhism in Andhra.
Exam Note:

• Capital – Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda)
• Greatest Patron of Buddhism – Veerapurushadatta

s: Which Vishnukundin ruler had transferred the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?
x:
The Vishnukundins emerged as an important dynasty in the Deccan after the decline of the Ikshvakus and the Salankayanas. Their early capital was Amarapuri (identified with Amaravati region). As the kingdom expanded towards the coastal Andhra region, Madhavavarma II shifted the capital to Denduluru (near present-day Eluru in West Godavari district). This strategic shift enabled better control over the fertile Vengi region and facilitated administration of the eastern coastal territories. Madhavavarma II was the most powerful ruler of the dynasty. He assumed the title Janasraya, performed several Vedic sacrifices such as the Ashvamedha, and greatly expanded the kingdom. Why the other options are incorrect:
Option (1): Vikramendravarma – He was an important Vishnukundin ruler but is not credited with shifting the capital to Denduluru.
Option (3): Govindavarma – Founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty. During his reign, the capital remained at Amarapuri.
Option (4): Manchana Bhattaraka – A later ruler who ruled during the declining phase of the dynasty and did not shift the capital.
Exam Note:
• Founder – Govindavarma
• Greatest ruler – Madhavavarma II (Janasraya)
• Early Capital – Amarapuri
• Later Capital – Denduluru

Reason (R): No ruler had issued coins with ship motif after Satavahanas.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

x:
Assertion (A): "Trade with Rome flourished in the post-Satavahana era." This statement is false. Indo-Roman trade reached its peak during the Satavahana period (1st Century BCE–2nd Century CE). After the decline of the Roman Empire in the West and the fall of the Satavahanas, trade with Rome gradually declined. Although overseas trade continued with Southeast Asia and other regions, Roman trade no longer flourished during the post-Satavahana period.
Reason (R): "No ruler had issued coins with ship motif after Satavahanas." This statement is true. The Satavahanas were famous for issuing coins bearing the ship motif, symbolising their active maritime trade. No later Andhra dynasty is known to have issued coins featuring this motif. Since the Assertion is false and the Reason is true, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Satavahana ports – Ghantasala, Dharanikota, Kottapatnam, Motupalli (later prominence)
• Roman gold coins have been discovered at several Satavahana sites.

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect?
a. Billa Surgam Palaeolithic cave site is located in Anantapuramu district.
b. Belum caves located in Nandyal district is the second longest cave in India.
c. Cave sites of Kurnool and Muchatla Chintamani Gavi in Andhra Pradesh are the only places in India where tools made of animal bones were found in Upper Palaeolithic context.
Options:
x:
Let us examine each statement separately.
Statement (a): "Billa Surgam Palaeolithic cave site is located in Anantapuramu district." This statement is incorrect. The famous Billa Surgam Caves are located in Kurnool district (present administrative region falls under Nandyal district after district reorganisation), not in Anantapuramu. These caves are internationally significant because they have yielded evidence of prehistoric human occupation.
Statement (b): "Belum Caves located in Nandyal district is the second longest cave in India." This statement is correct. Belum Caves are located in Nandyal district and are the second longest natural cave system in India, after Krem Liat Prah in Meghalaya.
Statement (c): "Cave sites of Kurnool and Muchatla Chintamani Gavi are the only places in India where tools made of animal bones were found in Upper Palaeolithic context." This statement is correct. Archaeological excavations have revealed bone tools from these cave sites, making them unique in the Indian prehistoric context. Therefore, only statement (a) is incorrect.
Exam Note:
• Billa Surgam Caves – Kurnool/Nandyal region
• Belum Caves – Nandyal district
• Belum Caves – Second longest natural cave system in India
• Bone tools – Kurnool cave sites are unique in India

s: Which of the following statements is not true about the Satavahanas?

Therefore, any matrimonial alliance between them is historically impossible. Why the other options are correct:
Option (1): Correct. The Puranas refer to the Satavahanas as Andhra Bhrityas.
Option (2): Correct. Some Satavahana coins carry legends in Prakrit (Brahmi script) and early Dravidian (Tamil) language, especially those issued for circulation in the southern regions.
Option (3): Correct. The Satavahanas patronised both Brahmanical religion (Hinduism) and Buddhism. Kings performed Vedic sacrifices while queens, merchants and officials donated generously to Buddhist monasteries and stupas such as Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Nannaya Bhattu are correct? I. Nannaya Bhattu was a Telugu poet and the author of Andhra Mahabharatam, a Telugu retelling of the Sanskrit Mahabharata. Statement II: Correct. Nannaya is traditionally credited with writing Andhra Shabda Chintamani, the earliest known Sanskrit treatise on Telugu grammar. Although the original work is no longer available, later scholars have frequently referred to it.
Statement III: Correct. An inscription records that Raja Raja Narendra granted Nandampudi Agrahara to Nannaya in recognition of his literary scholarship and service. Since all three statements are correct, the answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Nannaya – Adi Kavi of Telugu literature
• Patron – Raja Raja Narendra

s: The architectural structure of which of the following temples exemplifies the independent style of the Chalukya-Cholas, incorporating Pallava and early Chalukya influences?
x:
The Draksharama Bhimeswara Temple represents the mature architectural style developed under the Chalukya-Cholas. Its design combines features of Pallava architecture, such as elegant structural planning, with Early Chalukyan elements, resulting in a distinctive regional style. This fusion later influenced temple architecture across the Godavari region. The Brihadeeshwara Temple at Thanjavur is a masterpiece of Imperial Chola architecture and does not represent the independent Chalukya-Chola style. The Padmakshi Temple at Hanamkonda is associated primarily with the Kakatiyas and reflects Kakatiya architectural traditions rather than Chalukya-Chola architecture. Therefore, Draksharama Temple is the correct answer.
Exam Note:
• Draksharama – Chalukya-Chola style
• Brihadeeshwara – Imperial Chola style
• Padmakshi – Kakatiya architecture

s: Which of the following statements regarding Kakatiyas are correct? I. Early Kakatiya monarchs had constructed Jain temples. II. The influence of Chalukya temple architecture could be seen in Kakatiya temples. III. Thousand Pillared Temple was built in Trikuta style, having three shrines, each dedicated to Rudreshwara, Vasudeva and Suryadeva.
x:
All the three statements are correct. The early Kakatiya rulers were followers of Jainism before gradually embracing Shaivism. As a result, several Jain temples and basadis were constructed during the early phase of Kakatiya rule. The famous Padmakshi Temple at Hanamkonda is believed to have originally been a Jain shrine before later becoming a Hindu temple. Kakatiya temple architecture evolved under the influence of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani. Features such as intricately carved pillars, star-shaped platforms, ornate doorways and finely sculptured ceilings clearly reflect Chalukyan influence while developing into a distinct Kakatiya architectural style. The famous Thousand Pillared Temple at Hanamkonda, constructed during the reign of Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) in 1163 CE, is built in the Trikuta style. It contains three sanctums dedicated to Rudreshwara (Shiva), Vasudeva (Vishnu) and Suryadeva (Sun God). It is regarded as one of the finest examples of Kakatiya architecture. Hence, all three statements are correct and the answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Early religion of Kakatiyas – Jainism
• Later religion – Shaivism
• Thousand Pillared Temple – Hanamkonda (1163 CE)
• Built by – Rudradeva

Reason (R) is true. The Nizam of Hyderabad, Afzal-ud-Dowla (Asaf Jah V), remained loyal to the British during the Revolt of 1857. His cooperation helped the British suppress revolutionary activities in the Deccan and prevented the uprising from spreading widely in the Hyderabad State. The loyalty of the Nizam was one of the important reasons for the failure of the revolt in the Deccan. Since the Assertion is false and the Reason is true, the correct answer is Option (4).

The Eastern Ghats extend discontinuously through the northern districts of Andhra Pradesh. In Srikakulam district, these hill ranges are known as Mahendra Girulu (Mahendragiri Hills). These hills form part of the Eastern Ghats and extend into the neighbouring state of Odisha. Mahendragiri is associated with several historical and mythological traditions. The other hill ranges belong to different regions of Andhra Pradesh. s: Arrange the following in chronological order: A. Formation of the Visalandra Mahasabha B. Dhar Commission C. Swami Sitaram's fast D. Formation of States Re-organization Commission
x:
The demand for a separate Andhra State and later a Visalandhra gained momentum after Independence through a series of political developments. The Dhar Commission was appointed in 1948 to examine the question of linguistic provinces. It did not recommend the formation of states on a linguistic basis. In 1949, the Visalandra Mahasabha was formed to campaign for the unification of all Telugu-speaking areas into a single state. Swami Sitaram undertook his fast in 1951 demanding the formation of Andhra State, which further intensified the movement. The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) was constituted in 1953 under the chairmanship of Justice Fazl Ali to examine the reorganisation of states on linguistic and administrative grounds. Its recommendations eventually led to the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956. Thus, the correct chronological order is: Dhar Commission → Visalandra Mahasabha → Swami Sitaram's Fast → States Reorganisation Commission Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Dhar Commission – 1948
• Visalandra Mahasabha – 1949
• Swami Sitaram's Fast – 1951
• States Reorganisation Commission – 1953

s: Arrange the following events chronologically: A. Implementation of Ryotwari Settlement in Madras B. Acquisition of Guntur by East India Company C. Battle of Padmanabham D. Abolition of Zamindari Settlement in Andhra
x:
The East India Company acquired Guntur in 1788, making it the earliest event among the four. The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794 between the British East India Company and the Vizianagaram Zamindar, Maharaja Vijayarama Gajapati Raju. The British emerged victorious, further strengthening their control over the Northern Circars. The Ryotwari Settlement, introduced by Sir Thomas Munro, was gradually implemented in the Madras Presidency during the early nineteenth century, beginning around 1802 and expanding thereafter. Under this system, revenue was collected directly from cultivators rather than through Zamindars. The Zamindari System was abolished after Independence through the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, which came into force in the following years. Thus, the correct chronological order is: Acquisition of Guntur → Battle of Padmanabham → Ryotwari Settlement → Abolition of Zamindari Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Guntur acquired – 1788
• Battle of Padmanabham – 1794
• Ryotwari System – Sir Thomas Munro
• Zamindari Abolition – Post-Independence

s: Manchikallu and Maidavolu inscriptions belong to
x:
The Manchikallu and Maidavolu inscriptions are among the earliest inscriptions of the Pallavas in the Andhra region. They are particularly important because they provide valuable evidence regarding the early history, genealogy and territorial expansion of the Pallava dynasty. The Maidavolu inscription, issued in Prakrit, belongs to Sivaskandavarman, one of the earliest known Pallava rulers. Along with the Hirahadagalli inscription, it is an important source for reconstructing the political history of the early Pallavas. The Manchikallu inscription also belongs to the early Pallava period and confirms Pallava authority in the Andhra region before their expansion into Tamil Nadu. Therefore, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note: Important Early Pallava Inscriptions:
• Maidavolu Inscription
• Manchikallu Inscription

a. Vignana Chandrika Grandhamandali I. Kovvur, 1916
b. Srikrishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam II. Hyderabad, 1906
c. Andhra Council of Research III. Hyderabad, 1901
d. Andhra Saraswati Parishad IV. Hyderabad, 1922
x:
The Srikrishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam, established in Hyderabad in 1901, was one of the earliest Telugu libraries in the Hyderabad State. It played a crucial role in promoting Telugu language and literature. The Vignana Chandrika Grandhamandali was founded in Hyderabad in 1906 to publish books and encourage intellectual activity among Telugu-speaking people. The Andhra Council of Research was established at Kovvur in 1916 with the objective of encouraging historical and literary research relating to Andhra. The Andhra Saraswati Parishad, founded in Hyderabad in 1922, became an important institution for promoting Telugu language, literature and education. Thus, the correct matching is a–II, b–III, c–I, d– IV, corresponding to Option (3).
Exam Note: Prominent libraries and literary bodies established across Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema:
• Saraswathi Mahal Library (Thanjavur, 1700s): While located in Tamil Nadu, it holds one of the most vital historical collections of ancient Telugu palm-leaf manuscripts preserved by the Raghunatha Nayaka kings.
• Gautami Regional Library / Gautami Grandhalayam (Rajahmundry, 1898): Formed by merging the Vasuraya Grandhalayam and the Town Hall Library. It is one of the oldest public libraries in the state.
• The Reading Club (Kolluru, Guntur, 1899): One of the earliest rural library initiatives in the Guntur district.
• Youngmen's Literary Association (Guntur, 1900): Created to foster intellectual dialogue and provide access to newspapers and nationalist literature.
• Vardhamana Samajam (Nellore, 1906): An influential library and socio-cultural center that powered the library movement in the Nellore region.
• Sri Rammohan Library (Vijayawada, 1911): Founded by Ayyanki Venkata Ramanaiah, the architect of the Public Library Movement in India.
• Saraswathi Niketanam (Vetapalem, Bapatla, 1911): Established by V.V. Shreshti, it is famous for housing a rare collection of century-old periodicals, gazettes, and historical books.
• Andhra Sahitya Parishad (Kakinada, 1911): Originally established in Madras in 1911 to protect and publish Telugu linguistic texts, its operations and massive manuscript library permanently moved to Kakinada in 1922.
• Andhra Pradesh Library Association (Vijayawada, 1914): Founded at Rammohan Library, it is the oldest state library association in India and gave birth to the Indian library movement.
• Andhra Council of Research (Kovvur, 1916): Formed specifically to collect, preserve, and conduct historical research on ancient Telugu manuscripts and literature.
• Andhra Grandhalayam (Kurnool, 1920): Established by Mocharla Ramachandra Rao to serve as a pivotal library hub for the Rayalaseema region.
• Sarada Grandhalayam (Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, 1936): Founded by the Korukonda brothers on Gandhian principles, serving as an active nationalist study circle during the freedom struggle.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Library Movement are correct? I. In 1915, the Andhra Desa Library Association started a periodical entitled 'Grandhalaya Sarvasvam' in Telugu. II. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao is the founder of Andhra Patrika, established in 1908. III. Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was established in Kovvur in 1916. IV. In 1918, Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao started Boat Library Services in West Godavari.
x:
Statement I is correct. The Andhra Desa Library Association launched the Telugu periodical Grandhalaya Sarvasvam in 1915 to promote the library movement and spread reading habits among the people.
Statement II is correct. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao Pantulu founded the famous Telugu newspaper Andhra Patrika in 1908. It became one of the most influential newspapers during the Indian National Movement and played a vital role in awakening political consciousness among Telugu-speaking people.
Statement III is incorrect. Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was not established at Kovvur in 1916. It was established in Hyderabad in 1901. The institution established at Kovvur in 1916 was the Andhra Council of Research.
Statement IV is correct. In 1918, Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao introduced the innovative Boat Library Service in the Godavari region to carry books to villages located along riverbanks, thereby expanding access to education and reading. Therefore, Statements I, II and IV are correct, making Option (1) the correct answer.
Exam Note:
• Andhra Patrika – Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao (1908)
• Grandhalaya Sarvasvam – 1915
• Boat Library Service – Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao (1918)
• Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam – Hyderabad (1901)

s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect?
a. Communist Party leaders worked for the Visalandhra Movement and propagated the concept of Visalandhra even before the formation of Andhra State.
b. Communists became a great force in Telangana politics.
c. Communists opposed the formation of integrated linguistic States.
x:
Statement (a) is correct. The Communist Party strongly supported the demand for Visalandhra, advocating the unification of all Telugu-speaking areas into a single linguistic state even before the formation of Andhra State in 1953. Communist leaders regarded linguistic states as a means of strengthening democratic administration and promoting regional development.
Statement (b) is correct. The Communists emerged as a powerful political force in Telangana, particularly during the Telangana Armed Struggle (1946–1951) against the feudal system under the Nizam. Their leadership among peasants and agricultural labourers gave them significant political influence in the region.
Statement (c) is incorrect. The Communist Party did not oppose the formation of integrated linguistic states. On the contrary, it consistently supported the creation of linguistic states and strongly advocated the formation of Visalandhra by merging Andhra State with the Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State. Therefore, only Statement (c) is incorrect. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Communist Party – Strong supporter of Visalandhra.
• Telangana Armed Struggle (1946–1951) significantly strengthened Communist influence in Telangana.

The Gentlemen's Agreement, signed in 1956 before the formation of Andhra Pradesh, was intended to safeguard the interests of the Telangana region after its merger with Andhra State. One of its important provisions related to the composition of the State Cabinet. It provided that the Cabinet should consist of ministers in the ratio of 60:40 between Andhra and Telangana, reflecting the relative population of the two regions while ensuring adequate representation for Telangana. The Agreement also included safeguards relating to public employment, expenditure, education and the establishment of the Telangana Regional Committee. Therefore, the correct answer is Option (3).

s: Who was the first Telugu writer to win the Jnanpith Award for the work titled "Ramayana Kalpavriksham"?
x:
Viswanatha Satyanarayana became the first Telugu writer to receive the Jnanpith Award, India's highest literary honour, for his monumental work Ramayana Kalpavriksham. The work is regarded as one of the greatest literary reinterpretations of the Ramayana in Telugu and reflects Viswanatha's profound scholarship, classical style and philosophical depth. Besides this masterpiece, he authored numerous novels, poems, dramas and literary essays, making him one of the most prolific writers in Telugu literature. Later, Dr. C. Narayana Reddy also received the Jnanpith Award for his poetic work Viswambhara, but he was not the first Telugu recipient. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:

s: In which year was the English East India Company established?
x:
The English East India Company was established on 31 December 1600 when Queen Elizabeth I granted a Royal Charter to a group of English merchants under the name "The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies." The Company was initially formed for trade with the East Indies, particularly in spices, silk, cotton textiles and other valuable commodities. Over time, it expanded its commercial activities in India by establishing trading factories at Surat (1613), Machilipatnam (1611), Madras (1639), Bombay (1668) and Calcutta (1690). Gradually, the Company transformed itself from a commercial organization into a political power. Following the Battle of Plassey (1757) and the Battle of Buxar (1764), it acquired territorial control over large parts of India. Company rule continued until 1858, when, after the Revolt of 1857, administration was transferred directly to the British Crown through the Government of India Act, 1858. Therefore, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Established – 31 December 1600
• Charter Granted by – Queen Elizabeth I
• End of Company Rule – 1858

x:
Yanam, situated on the banks of the Godavari River in present-day Andhra Pradesh, was an important French settlement in India. It formed part of French India, along with Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahé and Chandernagore. The French established their trading settlement at Yanam during the eighteenth century and used it as an important commercial centre for trade in textiles and agricultural products. Although India became independent in 1947, Yanam continued under French administration until 1954, when it was de facto transferred to India. The legal transfer (de jure) took place in 1962. Today, Yanam forms part of the Union Territory of Puducherry. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).

The earliest inscriptions of the Satavahanas have been discovered mainly in Maharashtra, indicating that the dynasty initially established its political base in the western Deccan before expanding eastward into Andhra. Important early Satavahana inscriptions include those found at Naneghat and Nasik, both located in present-day Maharashtra. The Naneghat Inscription, issued by Queen Naganika, wife of Satakarni I, provides valuable information about the genealogy of the early Satavahana rulers and the Vedic sacrifices performed by the king. Similarly, the Nasik Cave Inscriptions, particularly that of Gautami Balasri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni, are among the most important sources for Satavahana political history. Although the Satavahanas later ruled large parts of Andhra Pradesh and contributed significantly to the development of Amaravati and Dharanikota, their earliest inscriptional evidence comes from Maharashtra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).

The growing demand for a separate university gained momentum through the efforts of Telugu intellectuals, educationists and public leaders. Responding to these demands, the Andhra University Act was passed in 1925, and the University was formally established in 1926. Initially, the University functioned from Bezwada (Vijayawada) and was later shifted to Waltair (Visakhapatnam), where it continues to be one of the premier educational institutions in the country. It consists of Right View, Right Resolve, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness and Right Concentration. Shaivism is centred on the worship of Lord Shiva, whose most important symbol is the Shiva Linga, representing both creation and cosmic energy. Animism refers to the belief that natural objects such as mountains, rivers, trees and animals possess spiritual power. Hence, Nature Worship is its defining characteristic. To implement this policy, the Portuguese developed a strong navy, built coastal forts and attempted to eliminate Arab and other European competitors from maritime trade. Gatha Saptasati (Gaha Sattasai), compiled by the Satavahana ruler King Hala, is regarded as the most important literary source for understanding the socio-cultural life of the Satavahana period. Written in Maharashtri Prakrit, the work consists of nearly 700 verses, most of which deal with the everyday life of ordinary people rather than royal exploits. The poems vividly portray family life, marriage customs, status of women, agriculture, trade, village economy, festivals, occupations and social relationships. They provide valuable insights into the customs, beliefs and emotions of people living during the Satavahana age. Unlike political inscriptions, which mainly record donations and victories, Gatha Saptasati reflects the social and cultural environment of the period. For this reason, historians consider it the most important literary source for reconstructing Satavahana society. Although the Puranas provide genealogical information about the Satavahanas, they do not describe the social life in such detail. Similarly, Aitareya Brahmana and Dharmasutras belong to much earlier periods and have no direct connection with Satavahana society. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).

• Language – Maharashtri Prakrit
• Contents – Around 700 verses

s: When was the Gentlemen's Agreement signed?
x:
The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed on 20 February 1956 between the leaders of Andhra State and Telangana. The agreement provided safeguards for Telangana regarding employment, education, expenditure and political representation before the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Gentlemen's Agreement – 20 February 1956 The 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement was signed by 8 key political leaders representing the Andhra and Telangana regions on February 20, 1956, to safeguard Telangana's interests prior to the formation of unified Andhra Pradesh. Signatories from Andhra Region
• Bezwada Gopal Reddy – Chief Minister of Andhra State
• Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy – Andhra Congress leader (later Chief Minister and President of India)
• Gouthu Latchanna – Andhra leader and minister
• Alluri Satyanarayana Raju – Andhra Congress committee leader Signatories from Telangana (Hyderabad State) Region
• Burgula Ramakrishna Rao – Chief Minister of Hyderabad State
• K. V. Ranga Reddy – Telangana political leader
• Marri Channa Reddy – Telangana leader (later Chief Minister of undivided AP)
• J. V. Narasing Rao The key provisions ensured financial protection, job security, and regional autonomy for Telangana. Finances and Development
• Surplus Revenue: Extra money earned from the Telangana region must be spent only on the development of Telangana.
• Shared Expenses: State administration costs were to be split proportionally between the two regions. Jobs and Education
• Mulki Rules: Local job and education rules were kept, meaning only people who lived in Telangana for a set time could get local government jobs.
• Educational Safeguards: School and college seats in Telangana were reserved for students from Telangana. Governance and Power
• Regional Committee: A special committee of Telangana assembly members was formed to look after regional development, planning, and local rules.
• Cabinet Balance: The state cabinet was to have a fair number of ministers from both the Telangana and Andhra regions.
• The Actual Ratio: The official Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 stipulated a 60:40 ratio for Cabinet representation.
• The Distribution: This mandated that 60% of the cabinet ministers were to be from the Andhra region and 40% from the Telangana region, reflecting the respective population and assembly sizes at the time.
• The Leadership Rule: If the Chief Minister was chosen from Andhra, the Deputy Chief Minister position had to go to a leader from Telangana, and vice versa
